attempts.plan:
1. Read the CSV (33 rows) into a pandas DataFrame containing: borough, first_half_2015_value, second_half_2015_value.  
2. Handle missing values (1 in each column): drop any borough that has a missing value in EITHER time-period column, because both numbers are required to compute its change. This will reduce the working-set size from 33 to either 32 or 31 rows, depending on whether the two missing entries belong to the same borough or different ones.  
3. Compute the change variable for every retained borough: Δ = second_half_2015_value – first_half_2015_value.  
4. Build an N × N binary spatial-weights matrix W from the neighbor list provided: W_ij = 1 if borough i is listed as a neighbor of borough j (treat the relationship as symmetric), otherwise 0; set the diagonal to 0.  
5. Row-standardize W so that every row sums to 1 (skip any row that would be all zeros; those rows will remain all zeros after standardization).  
6. Calculate the Global Moran’s I statistic for the change vector Δ using formula:  
   I = (N / Σ_i Σ_j W_ij) * (Σ_i Σ_j W_ij (Δ_i – ȳ)(Δ_j – ȳ)) / Σ_i (Δ_i – ȳ)²  
   where ȳ is the mean of Δ and N is the number of boroughs after dropping missing cases.  
7. Assess statistical significance with a permutation test:  
   a. Randomly shuffle the Δ values across boroughs 999 times (≥500 as required).  
   b. Recalculate Moran’s I for each shuffle to build the null distribution.  
   c. The p-value is the proportion of permutations whose I is as extreme or more extreme than the observed I (two-tailed).  
8. Interpret results:  
   • If observed I is positive and p < 0.05, conclude “CLUSTERED” (similar-direction changes cluster spatially).  
   • If observed I is negative and p < 0.05, report “DISPERSED”.  
   • Otherwise, p ≥ 0.05 → conclude “NOT CLUSTERED”.  
9. Report the observed Moran’s I and the permutation-based p-value in the required single-line format.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------
# 1. Load the two supplied files
# ------------------------------
DATA_PATH = "chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_no2crime_crime_first_half_2015_to_second_half_2015.csv"
ADJ_PATH  = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

crime = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)
adj   = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)

# -------------------------------------------------
# 2. Drop any borough with a missing crime reading
# -------------------------------------------------
crime = crime.dropna(subset=["first_half_2015_value", "second_half_2015_value"])
crime["delta"] = crime["second_half_2015_value"] - crime["first_half_2015_value"]
crime.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)

# keep only the boroughs that survived the NA-drop in the adjacency list
kept_boroughs = set(crime["borough"])
adj = adj[adj["borough"].isin(kept_boroughs) & adj["neighbor"].isin(kept_boroughs)]

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Build a symmetric binary adjacency (spatial-weights) matrix
# -------------------------------------------------------------
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(crime["borough"])}
N = len(crime)
W = np.zeros((N, N), dtype=float)

# fill W with 1 where adjacency exists
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row["borough"]]
    j = borough_to_idx[row["neighbor"]]
    W[i, j] = 1
    W[j, i] = 1          # enforce symmetry

# -------------------------------------------------
# 4. Row-standardise   (each row sums to 1, if > 0)
# -------------------------------------------------
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
# avoid division by zero for isolated boroughs
row_sums[row_sums == 0] = 1
W = W / row_sums

# -------------------------------------------------
# 5. Compute Global Moran's I for the change vector
# -------------------------------------------------
y = crime["delta"].values
y_mean = y.mean()
y_diff = y - y_mean
denom = np.sum(y_diff**2)
num   = np.sum(W * np.outer(y_diff, y_diff))
W_sum = W.sum()

I_obs = (N / W_sum) * (num / denom)

# -------------------------------------------------
# 6. Permutation test (999 random label shuffles)
# -------------------------------------------------
np.random.seed(0)
permutations = 999
I_perm = np.empty(permutations)

for p in range(permutations):
    y_perm = np.random.permutation(y)
    y_diff_p = y_perm - y_perm.mean()
    denom_p  = np.sum(y_diff_p**2)
    num_p    = np.sum(W * np.outer(y_diff_p, y_diff_p))
    I_perm[p] = (N / W_sum) * (num_p / denom_p)

# two-tailed p-value
p_val = (np.sum(np.abs(I_perm) >= abs(I_obs)) + 1) / (permutations + 1)  # +1 for observed itself

# -------------------------------------------------
# 7. Verdict
# -------------------------------------------------
verdict = "CLUSTERED" if (I_obs > 0) and (p_val < 0.05) else "NOT CLUSTERED"

# -----------------------
# 8. Required printouts
# -----------------------
print(f"data_points_used = {N}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (Moran_I = {I_obs:.4f}, p = {p_val:.4f})")
